channel.title: Kseniia's Good News
channel.description: Positive news from several sources, scored 0-10 for goodness and refreshed every six hours.

item.title: Indian designer makes building tiles from recovered air-pollution carbon [7/10]
item.description: Carbon Craft Design turns carbon waste recovered from pollution into eco-friendly tiles, giving it a second use. (Goodness 7/10: Creative reuse of pollution, scale still to be shown.)

item.title: Rohingya refugees use agroforestry to restore degraded land in Bangladesh [7/10]
item.description: Families in Kutupalong camp combine farming projects with traditional agroecology to bring back degraded landscape around the camp. (Goodness 7/10: Restores land and livelihoods for a displaced community.)

item.title: Aerial photos show Florida Bay recovering as Everglades restoration advances [7/10]
item.description: More freshwater flowing under Everglades restoration is linked to returning wading birds and waterfowl in Florida Bay. (Goodness 7/10: Visible ecological recovery from a long-running restoration.)

item.title: Whale populations recover in Argentine waters after whaling bans [7/10]
item.description: Humpback and other whale populations are returning to Patagonia, though they now face new pressures such as shipping and fishing. (Goodness 7/10: Clear recovery success, tempered by emerging threats.)

item.title: Researchers turn discarded PVC into a material for high-performance engines [6/10]
item.description: Virginia Tech scientists converted waste PVC, a hard-to-recycle plastic, into a material usable in demanding engine applications. (Goodness 6/10: Promising recycling route, but still a research result.)

item.title: Football tournament helps 30 Nagaland villages agree to ban pangolin hunting [7/10]
item.description: Community initiatives in Nagaland, Manipur and Gujarat, including a tournament that united 30 villages, are protecting pangolins from hunting. (Goodness 7/10: Community-driven protection of a heavily trafficked species.)

item.title: Ladakh communities and conservationists reduce conflict with snow leopards [7/10]
item.description: Predator-proof livestock corrals and homestays in Ladakh help villagers live alongside snow leopards and earn income from conservation. (Goodness 7/10: Community-led coexistence benefits people and a vulnerable species.)

item.title: Women rangers help protect East Nimba Nature Reserve in Liberia [6/10]
item.description: A small group of women rangers patrols the reserve; only 17 of Liberia's 143 rangers are women. (Goodness 6/10: Positive profile, though women remain a small minority.)

item.title: Three lakh Indian students learn to code on their phones [6/10]
item.description: A visual story shows students across India learning to code on smartphones through an online platform. (Goodness 6/10: Wider access to skills, from a company-led story.)

item.title: Community forest titles in DR Congo rise from eight to over 350 [6/10]
item.description: Congolese community forest concessions have grown sharply since 2017, giving local people a stake in conservation, though funding hurdles remain. (Goodness 6/10: Real progress for local forest management, with obstacles left.)

item.title: Infant with aggressive brain cancer recovers after referral to St. Jude [7/10]
item.description: A baby given weeks to live is now cancer-free after her case reached a hospital that had just completed a study on her tumour type. (Goodness 7/10: Full recovery for one child, though the result depends on specialist access.)

item.title: Biovac plans larger African vaccine production by 2028 [7/10]
item.description: South Africa's Biovac says a new facility aims to substantially increase vaccine production in Africa by the end of 2028. (Goodness 7/10: Could improve vaccine access, but not yet delivered.)

item.title: Sierra Leone's maternal mortality falls steeply over 20 years [8/10]
item.description: Maternal deaths have fallen considerably over two decades, though unofficial fees, mistrust and poor infrastructure still hinder care. (Goodness 8/10: Real progress for many lives, with challenges remaining.)

item.title: India's Venice Biennale exhibition wins Visitors' Lion [6/10]
item.description: India's exhibition, made by five artists using materials such as bamboo and thread, won the public-voted Visitors' Lion for Best National Participation. (Goodness 6/10: Cultural recognition for artists and a country.)

item.title: Scientists describe five new horned frog species in Arunachal Pradesh [6/10]
item.description: Researchers from the University of Delhi and Harvard identified five new horned frog species in northeast India. (Goodness 6/10: New species add to knowledge, though discovery alone does not protect them.)

item.title: Portland nonprofit turns rescued food into prepared meals [7/10]
item.description: Urban Gleaners rescues food before it is wasted and cooks donated ingredients into meals for hungry residents in Portland. (Goodness 7/10: Cuts food waste and feeds people locally.)

item.title: Women farmers cultivate endangered Himalayan medicinal plants [7/10]
item.description: Women in Uttarakhand are growing endangered high-altitude plants such as kutki, easing overharvesting in alpine meadows. (Goodness 7/10: Community-led conservation that also supports livelihoods.)

item.title: One million Deccan Mahseer released into Ujani reservoir [7/10]
item.description: BNHS with Cipla Foundation and Tata Power released 10 lakh native fish as part of a ten-year effort to restore the once-rare species. (Goodness 7/10: Large long-term restoration effort for a threatened fish.)

item.title: Former egg collectors now guard Malaysia's endangered river terrapin nests [8/10]
item.description: In Terengganu, ex-egg collectors patrol riverbanks as Terrapin Guardians, having incubated 13,224 eggs and released over 8,200 hatchlings. (Goodness 8/10: Measurable recovery effort for a critically endangered species.)

item.title: Lula recognizes Indigenous territory of Chief Raoni's peoples [7/10]
item.description: Brazil's president signed an order recognizing the Mebêngôkre and Yudjá peoples' permanent right to the 362,000-hectare Kapôt Nhĩnore territory; further steps remain. (Goodness 7/10: Significant land-rights step, but formal recognition is not complete.)

item.title: Stolen 13th-century Virgin carving recovered after nearly 50 years [6/10]
item.description: Detectives have recovered a Romanesque Virgin Mary sculpture stolen in 1979 from a church in Navarre, Spain. (Goodness 6/10: A lost heritage object returns home, a local rather than broad benefit.)

item.title: Seabirds Fitted With Sensors to Monitor the Ocean [6/10]
item.description: Researchers fitted seabirds with audio recorders and tracking devices to monitor activity across the ocean. (Goodness 6/10: Animal-borne sensors can improve ocean monitoring with low impact.)

item.title: Atlantic nations adopt new shark finning rules [6/10]
item.description: ICCAT members agreed a compromise that could require sharks to keep fins naturally attached by 2029 or 2030, with temporary exceptions for frozen catch. (Goodness 6/10: Progress for sharks, though weaker than conservationists wanted.)

item.title: Rabat Festival Showcases African and Middle Eastern Musicians [6/10]
item.description: The 13th Visa For Music festival in Rabat presented 28 live showcases by African and Middle Eastern musicians. (Goodness 6/10: A cultural event connecting musicians across regions.)

item.title: Texas couple refurbishes donated cars and gives them to neighbours in need [6/10]
item.description: An auto-repair couple in Texas repairs donated vehicles and hands them to neighbours who lack transport, helping people reach work and appointments. (Goodness 6/10: Direct, local help, though limited in scale.)

item.title: Land Returned to Native American Ownership in Massachusetts [7/10]
item.description: The Nature Conservancy has transferred about 126 acres of salt marsh and habitat in Eastham, Massachusetts, to Native American ownership and care. (Goodness 7/10: Land return gives Indigenous stewards a coastal habitat, though it is a small parcel.)

item.title: Global Seed Vault in the Arctic Safeguards Crop Diversity [6/10]
item.description: More than a million seed samples are stored in the Global Seed Vault in the Norwegian Arctic to support future food systems. (Goodness 6/10: A long-term safeguard for food crops, though it is a storage effort rather than a new gain.)

item.title: Otters Return to Kuala Lumpur's Klang River [7/10]
item.description: Smooth-coated otters are increasingly seen along Kuala Lumpur's Klang River, raising hopes for the health of the city's waterway. (Goodness 7/10: Wildlife returning signals a recovering urban river.)

item.title: Ladakh village shares irrigation water through household rotas [7/10]
item.description: Families in Phey village in Ladakh take turns guarding water at night so that every farmer receives a fair share for irrigation. (Goodness 7/10: Local cooperation that secures water for a whole village.)

item.title: Study: Species Reduced to 50 Animals Can Recover, Usually With Help [6/10]
item.description: A study of 141 bird and mammal species that fell to 50 or fewer individuals found 61% recovered, though few did so without conservation help. (Goodness 6/10: Recovery is possible but usually depends on human help.)

item.title: Trial in Brazil links Wolbachia mosquito releases to 68% fewer viral infections [8/10]
item.description: A four-year trial releasing mosquitoes carrying Wolbachia bacteria in Brazil was linked to a 68% lower risk of mosquito-borne viral infections. (Goodness 8/10: Large real-world result that could protect many people from dengue-type diseases.)

item.title: Indigenous Women Plant Native Trees to Restore Water Sources in Bolivia [7/10]
item.description: Indigenous women in Bolivia's Tunari range are planting native Polylepis trees to restore forests and the water sources they protect. (Goodness 7/10: Community-led restoration protects local water supplies.)

item.title: Women in an Uttarakhand village revive 28 acres of barren land as forest [7/10]
item.description: Women in Manar village, led by Bhagirathi Devi, restored a degraded patch of land into forest and report no forest fires in over 20 years. (Goodness 7/10: Community-led restoration with lasting results.)

item.title: Schoolgirl Designs Solar-Powered Ironing Cart in India [6/10]
item.description: A schoolgirl designed a solar-powered ironing cart after seeing a street ironing vendor discard charcoal. (Goodness 6/10: A small, practical clean-energy idea that helps street workers.)

item.title: Surat student builds machine-learning tool to track India's groundwater [6/10]
item.description: Student Dheyay Shah built JALAAKAR, a machine-learning tool that uses data to better understand India's vanishing groundwater. (Goodness 6/10: Promising youth innovation, not yet proven at scale.)

item.title: Micronesian school accepts coconuts in place of tuition fees [6/10]
item.description: Faith Christian Academy in the Federated States of Micronesia lets families pay school costs with coconuts, so every islander can afford an education. (Goodness 6/10: Helps one community keep children in school, though the scale is local.)

item.title: Young entrepreneur pays Tamil Nadu weavers up to 35% more to sustain craft [6/10]
item.description: A 26-year-old entrepreneur pays Bhavani Jamakkalam weavers up to 35% more to keep the 300-year-old Tamil Nadu craft alive. (Goodness 6/10: Better pay supports a heritage craft and its artisans.)

item.title: Wild kiwi live in the Wellington hills again after 150 years [8/10]
item.description: Māori-led conservation work has brought wild kiwi back to the hills around Wellington for the first time in about 150 years. (Goodness 8/10: A clear species recovery led by the local community.)

item.title: India records a 38% drop in tuberculosis deaths [8/10]
item.description: Citing the WHO Global Tuberculosis Report 2026, India has seen tuberculosis deaths fall 38%, which the article attributes to public health efforts. (Goodness 8/10: Large national health gain affecting many lives.)

item.title: Mumbai network turns used clothes into income for workers [6/10]
item.description: The Textile Waste Innovation Network collects used clothes in Mumbai and routes them to reuse and recycling, creating income while keeping textiles out of landfill. (Goodness 6/10: A community-level recycling model that also supports livelihoods.)

item.title: China's mangrove cover more than doubled between 1998 and 2020 [7/10]
item.description: Researchers report that China's mangroves more than doubled in area from 1998 to 2020, and birds have returned to the restored habitat. (Goodness 7/10: Measured habitat recovery benefiting wildlife and coasts.)

item.title: One-of-a-Kind Refuge to 200,000 Walrus Protected Forever in Alaska [8/10]
item.description: Conservationists secured lasting protection for barrier islands off Point Lay, Alaska, where large numbers of Pacific walrus gather. (Goodness 8/10: Permanent protection of a key habitat for a large walrus population.)

item.title: Hyderabad Doctor Helps Cut Rare-Disease Drug Cost [8/10]
item.description: A Hyderabad doctor helped cut the cost of a rare-disease drug from about Rs 9 crore to roughly Rs 2.5 crore. (Goodness 8/10: Lower drug costs could widen access for patients with a rare disease.)

item.title: South African township turns shipping container into sensory therapy room [6/10]
item.description: Afrika Tikkun and Sensory-Space converted a recycled shipping container into a sensory therapy space for children in a township community. (Goodness 6/10: Low-cost therapy access for a community, at a small scale.)

item.title: Zambian farm closes its food-waste loop while supplying airline meals [6/10]
item.description: Loctaguna Organics, an agroecology farm near Lusaka, supplies produce to airline catering and recycles its food waste back into farming. (Goodness 6/10: Practical circular-farming model, still a single business.)

item.title: Wolves help spread wild blueberries, US study finds [6/10]
item.description: Blueberry seeds that passed through wolves sprouted faster and more often than seeds taken straight from the fruit, suggesting wolves aid plant dispersal. (Goodness 6/10: Research showing a benefit of predators for ecosystems, though a small study.)

item.title: Kerala researchers rescue 27,000 orchids from trees marked for felling [7/10]
item.description: Researchers in Kozhikode relocated 27,324 native orchids from roadside trees due to be cut, and 71% of the plants survived. (Goodness 7/10: A practical rescue with a high survival rate for native plants.)

item.title: Ember report: pairing wind with solar and batteries is most effective [7/10]
item.description: An Ember report finds that combining wind with solar and batteries works better for the grid than relying on either source alone. (Goodness 7/10: Useful evidence for clean energy planning.)

item.title: Song written by people touched by terminal illness is performed at Welsh hospice [6/10]
item.description: A song inspired by experiences of terminal illness, written by people affected by it, was performed for the first time at a hospice in Wales. (Goodness 6/10: A creative project that gives comfort to a small community.)

item.title: Indian-Built Surgical Robot Used in Beating-Heart Bypass [6/10]
item.description: Surgeons at Medanta Hospital performed a beating-heart bypass using an Indian-built surgical robot with five robotic arms. (Goodness 6/10: A domestic medical technology advance, with benefit so far limited to a few hospitals.)

item.title: Eurasian otters, once hunted for fur, return to Kashmir [7/10]
item.description: A new study documents recent sightings and field evidence of Eurasian otters reappearing in Kashmir after decades of hunting for their fur. (Goodness 7/10: A recovering species, though the study mostly documents presence rather than numbers.)

item.title: Spanish city that restricted cars in 1999 shows the results [7/10]
item.description: Pontevedra, Spain, has limited car traffic in its centre since 1999, which has led to cleaner air and a more pleasant city for residents. (Goodness 7/10: A long-running example that car-free centres work for residents.)

item.title: Two Delhi students turn classroom fans into air purifiers [6/10]
item.description: Two Delhi teenagers designed a filter costing about 140 rupees that fits over ordinary school fans, cleaning the air for around 200 pupils. (Goodness 6/10: A cheap, local fix for polluted classrooms, though small in scale.)

item.title: Otters seen regularly in Kuala Lumpur raise hopes for river recovery [6/10]
item.description: Smooth-coated otters are regularly seen in parts of Kuala Lumpur, including the Klang River, which conservationists take as a sign that urban waterways are improving. (Goodness 6/10: Wildlife returning to a city river is a modest but encouraging sign.)

item.title: Thumb joint replacement offered for severe arthritis [6/10]
item.description: A ball-and-socket thumb implant replaces the trapezium bone at the base of the thumb, treating severe arthritis much as hip or shoulder replacements do. (Goodness 6/10: A new surgical option for a painful, common condition, though still limited to severe cases.)

item.title: Karnataka women's group wins national award for saving indigenous seeds [7/10]
item.description: A self-help group of women farmers in Dharwad won a national award and ten lakh rupees for conserving more than 250 indigenous seed varieties. (Goodness 7/10: Protects crop diversity and recognises local farmers.)

item.title: Drug baxdrostat reverses hormone-driven high blood pressure in study [7/10]
item.description: A study of the FDA-approved drug baxdrostat found it reversed high blood pressure caused by excess hormone production in patients with the condition. (Goodness 7/10: Promising results for a common, hard-to-treat condition, though from a single study.)

item.title: Children's Hospital of New Orleans opens museum inside the hospital [6/10]
item.description: A young patient wanted a place for play and fresh air during treatment, and the hospital built a museum space for children to be distracted and enjoy time outdoors. (Goodness 6/10: A kind, local initiative that helps children in care.)

item.title: Assam village shifts from chasing elephants to feeding and mapping them [7/10]
item.description: Residents of Hatikhuli village in Assam changed their approach to wild elephants, feeding them and mapping their movements rather than driving them away. (Goodness 7/10: A community-led approach to coexistence with wildlife.)

item.title: IIT Roorkee team creates new spring to double village drinking water [7/10]
item.description: Researchers from IIT Roorkee located underground water and created a new spring in Unchaun village, Uttarakhand, raising drinking water supply in the lean season. (Goodness 7/10: Tangible water access for a village, and a method others could copy.)
